sections.label: GST tax administration amendments
sections.summary: The Bill contains three amendments: extending customer accounting, requiring electronic records and invoice details, and a $200 monthly penalty for late GST returns.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Bill contains three key amendments to improve tax administration.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: These are: (a) the extension of customer accounting to prescribed supplies commonly used in GST fraud; (b) the requirement for electronic record keeping and additional invoice details for selected businesses; and (c) the provision for the monthly penalty of $200 for late submission of GST returns to commence immediately after the due date for filing.

sections.label: Customer accounting for prescribed supplies
sections.summary: Customer accounting will apply to mobile phones sold without subscription plans, memory cards and off-the-shelf software.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: At this stage, customer accounting will be applicable for supplies of mobile phones sold without mobile subscription plans, memory cards and off-the-shelf software.

sections.label: Monthly penalty for late GST returns
sections.summary: A monthly penalty of $200 for late submission of GST returns will commence immediately after the filing due date.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Third, to deter late filing, we will provide for the monthly penalty of $200 for late submission of GST returns to commence immediately after the filing due date.

sections.label: Opt-out digital GST notices
sections.summary: An administrative change will provide the basis to implement an opt-out approach for digital GST notices.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Ms Indranee Rajah) (for the Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: Another administrative change will provide for the basis to implement an opt-out approach for digital GST notices.

sections.label: Late GST return penalty timing
sections.summary: The $200 monthly penalty for late GST returns, previously imposed a month after the due date, will commence immediately after the filing due date.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Another concern is that with the rise of scam and fraudulent activities on cyber platforms, such as emails, this could lead to another problem among those who are less informed.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: This then brings me to the next matter – the monthly penalty of $200 for late submission of GST returns.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Previously, this penalty was imposed on outstanding returns starting from a month after the filing due date.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: With the amendment, the penalty will commence immediately after the filing due date.

sections.label: Digital notices and SME late submission
sections.summary: The amendment makes digital notices the default and removes the one-month grace period; the Member asks whether SMEs are the majority of late submitters.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: (In Mandarin):   This amendment will make digital notices as the default mode of notification and, at the same time, take away the one-month grace period for late submission.

sentences.speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Can the Minister tell us whether SMEs account for the majority of companies that have late submission over the years?

sections.label: Suggestions received on Bill
sections.summary: Of 41 suggestions received, 30 were accepted with consequential revisions made to the draft text of the Bill.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Of the 41 suggestions received, 30 of which were accepted with consequential revisions made to the draft text of the Bill.

sections.label: GST Bill clause 9 penalty
sections.summary: A suggestion that the filing period be two months after the accounting period, as SMEs may have lesser resources and more difficulty meeting the deadline.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Thirdly, on clause 9 of the GST Bill to amend section 60 for the monthly penalty of $200 to kick in if GST is not filed within one month after the end of accounting period, instead of two months, to be equitable to taxpayers who pay on-time, perhaps consideration can be made for the filing period to be two months after the accounting period as SMEs may have lesser resources and more difficulty in meeting the deadline.

sections.label: IRAS tax arrears 2016
sections.summary: According to IRAS, tax arrears in 2016 were kept at 0.68% of net tax assessed, due to a focus on maximising voluntary compliance.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: According to IRAS, tax arrears in 2016 were kept at 0.68% of net tax assessed, and that this was due to a focus on maximising voluntary compliance.

sections.label: Singapore e-commerce GST proposals
sections.summary: A Temasek Holdings and Google report valued Singapore e-commerce at S$1.4 billion in 2015, projected to reach S$7.6 billion by 2020, with proposed GST changes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: A report by Temasek Holdings and Google showed that e-commerce in Singapore was valued at S$1.4 billion in 2015, with a projected hike to S$7.6 billion by 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Industry-watchers have proposed changes, such as requiring foreign e-commerce companies to register and charge GST for these cross-border transactions or reducing the current GST exemption on the import of goods worth $400 or less.

sections.label: GST filing and registration thresholds
sections.summary: 94% of GST returns are filed on time, and compulsory GST registration is required only for businesses with annual turnovers over $1 million.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: First, 94% of GST returns are filed on time, which shows that the majority of GST-registered businesses do not have problems complying with the filing due date.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Compulsory GST registration is only required for businesses that have annual turnovers of more than $1 million.

sections.label: Suggestions on customer accounting
sections.summary: Of the 41 suggestions received on the Bill, 30 suggestions or 73% were on customer accounting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: Of the 41 suggestions that we received on the Bill, 30 suggestions or 73% were on customer accounting.

sections.label: Customer accounting implementation postponed
sections.summary: The implementation date of customer accounting was postponed from 1 January 2018 to 1 January 2019 to help businesses cope with the change.

sentences.speaker: Ms Indranee Rajah
sentences.text: To help businesses cope with the change, we have postponed the implementation date of customer accounting from 1 January 2018 to 1 January 2019.
